order: This change declares two exceptions a round needs before it can close. The first covers the test-authoring seat, whose mirror substitution is unlawful by construction, because that seat is cast opposite the implementation author's family in every case, so a same-family substitution under outage cannot be permitted there. The router gets verified to carry no special-cased outage handling for that seat, so it falls through to the generic no-mirror path and lands at a wait status instead. The interface seat's plan names no authoring mirror for its primary role either, since closing stays its own order restricted to reads and the critic remains only a ceiling and not a substitution target. The lint script's exception check then gets extended to accept a declared cross-family exception, and it also accepts any no-mirror-for rung key, provided each one carries a reason string. The name-collision check gets extended too, so it finally scans the specialists directory as well.
claims: The two exceptions were declared directly in the casting table, and each one carries a reason string, exactly as the lint now requires. The lint script was extended to accept only a declared cross-family exception or a matching no-mirror-for rung key, nothing looser than that. The name-collision check now scans the specialists directory it had been missing, and exactly three files changed, with 100 insertions and 7 deletions in all. The router's casting behavior was traced and verified against the generic no-mirror path that governs the seat under outage.
